analysis: The Earth systems option is the strongest provisional match to the selected route. It develops geoscience, Earth systems, water management, climate, resource recovery and spatial analysis. Economics and qualitative and quantitative methods support questions about adaptation and policy. UCR lacks the same depth in ecology, plant-soil methods and successive disciplinary research projects. Stakeholder work in Research in a Sustainable Delta is a partial relation to consultancy, not a replacement for UvA’s four linked projects. Earth Observation is an appropriate counterpart to Remote Sensing. Living with Water relates to Water Management. Soil fieldwork, palaeoecology and ecotoxicology require separate comparator placements.

The technical option has coherent progression from Python and introductory data to algorithms and machine learning, then to optimisation, reinforcement learning and neural networks. AI Ethics is the clearest social or ethical contribution. The route has less social science and different project requirements than Bèta-gamma. The closest introductory Python pairing is DISGATE101; later machine learning supplies depth rather than a second pairing to the same introductory unit.

The cognition and society option combines brain and behaviour, developmental psychology, higher-order functions, and empirical methods with institutions and communication. Experimental methods strengthen the cognitive thread; strategy, rhetoric, documentary and history supply organisational and cultural contexts. There is no equivalent to the continuous major-project sequence. Higher Order Functions and Brain & Behavior overlap with Cognitie without exhausting its disciplinary range. BENGATE102 and GOSSOCI212 supply complementary overlap with the common research-methods course.

The final provisional schedules retain 24 distinct courses per option. The Earth option is strongest against the verified course list. AI and cognition are related academic directions grounded in the official major menu. The exact final display ordering and complete comparison remain dependent on verified progression.

BENECON312.contribution: Provides regression-based quantitative analysis for relationships among economic, social and spatial outcomes.

In this course you learn three estimators—Ordinary Least Squares, Generalized Least Squares, and Instrumental Variables—and three tests—t-test, F-test, and LM-test. Understanding the basic rules of econometrics, particularly the sampling distribution concept, is key, and the course uses Monte Carlo simulations in Stata to visualize it. Tools are applied to estimate economic relationships and make predictions, and students write an empirical paper.
